articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI chatbot got social engineered harder than a freshman at DEF CON, letting attackers hijack Instagram accounts including Obama's White House page. When your AI is dumber than a phishing email, maybe it's time to rethink that 'artificial intelligence' branding.

articles.title: Cheers to the Winners of EFF’s 18th Annual Cyberlaw Trivia Night!
articles.summary: CISA contractor dumped AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's a fucking recipe blog, exposing highly privileged government systems. The agency that's supposed to protect America's cyber infrastructure just handed the keys to anyone with a browser.

articles.title: Iran Signed a Ceasefire — Its Hackers Didn't
articles.summary: Trump's clown-car DNI appointment highlights why Section 702's warrantless mass surveillance needs to die in a fire. When the intelligence community is run by reality TV rejects, maybe we shouldn't give them unlimited spying powers.

articles.title: Ransomware sends Illinois high school on an early summer vacation
articles.summary: Ransomware crews had a month-long party with Check Point VPN zero-day CVE-2026-50751 before anyone bothered to patch it. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like letting the bad guys RSVP first.

articles.title: Oxford Uni student data pwned yet again - this time via career platform breach
articles.summary: NSO Group keeps targeting WhatsApp users despite a federal court telling them to fuck off, proving surveillance capitalism doesn't respect court orders. Meta's filing contempt charges because apparently some people need legal consequences explained in crayon.

articles.title: Frontier AI Models Can Find Crypto's Biggest Bugs. Experts Warn the Industry Isn't Ready
articles.summary: Cisco SD-WAN zero-day CVE-2026-20245 is being actively exploited with no patch in sight, because why fix critical infrastructure when you can just hope for the best? Also Windows Netlogon RCE is back like a bad sequel nobody asked for.

articles.title: DeFi’s old hack vectors are fading – But the new risk can hit six chains at once
articles.summary: AI models are now finding crypto bugs faster than human researchers, starting with a critical Zcash vulnerability discovered by Anthropic's Claude. The future is AI vs AI, and humans are just along for the ride to bankruptcy.

articles.title: CBSE retains COEMPT for answer-sheet scanning, shifts data to its own servers
articles.summary: Former IBM exec whistleblows the company for covering up years of Chinese state hacking because apparently corporate reputation matters more than national security. IBM's threat intelligence VP watched them bury breaches like it's fucking Watergate.

articles.title: NSO Group back in Meta's crosshairs after alleged WhatsApp targeting
articles.summary: GitHub nuked 70+ Microsoft repos after Miasma worm infections broke CI/CD pipelines everywhere, proving even Microsoft can't secure their own shit. The worm shapeshifts but its goal remains the same: hoover up cloud secrets like a digital vacuum cleaner.

articles.title: AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume: How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload
articles.summary: Check Point VPN users running deprecated IKEv1 are getting owned by CVE-2026-50751, a logic flaw that bypasses passwords entirely. Pro tip: maybe don't use protocols that were sketchy when Friendster was still a thing.
